enough to be noticeable in treated water.

**Possible Cause (initial assessment):** Likely algae bloom in the reservoir. Conditions over the
past week (rising turbidity, mild weather, stable water column) are consistent with algal growth.
Species identification pending – samples sent to lab for microscopy.

- Sampling frequency increased from 3x daily to 6x daily at NR-1 Intake.
- Additional parameter added: Algal Cell Count (initial count 4,200 cells/mL at 13:00, rising to
  5,100 cells/mL by 18:00).
- Treatment Works informed – monitoring final water quality closely.
- Lab requested to identify species and check for toxin-producing strains (e.g., *Microcystis*,
  *Anabaena*).

**Status:** Open – under investigation.

He reported that the routine maintenance programme for the current financial year was progressing well, with all scheduled tasks completed to date. He confirmed that the programme had been updated to reflect the findings of the annual condition assessment, and that the updated programme had been circulated to the Operations Director for review.

5.2 T. Hargreaves noted that the routine maintenance schedule was due for its annual review. He advised that the review would be completed by the end of June, and that any changes to the schedule would be reported to the board at the July meeting. He confirmed that the review would take into account the results of the spring inspection programme, which had been completed in early May.

**Present:** C. Whitfield (Chair), R. Alvarez (Vice-Chair), D. Thompson (Finance Director), T. Hargreaves (Engineering Director), P. Patel (Water Quality Manager), J. O'Neil (Operations Manager), S. Chen (Company Secretary), A. Mbeki (Non-Executive Director), L. Foster (Non-Executive Director)

**2. Minutes of the previous meeting**

2.1 The minutes of the meeting held on 19 February 2026 were approved as a correct record and signed by the Chair.

2.2 Matters arising not otherwise covered by the agenda:

- The Chair confirmed that the letter to the Environment Agency regarding the abstraction licence review had been sent on 2 March. A response was expected within the statutory 28-day window; no response had been received as of the date of this meeting.
- R. Alvarez confirmed that the meeting with the local residents' association regarding the Northgate reservoir landscaping works had taken place on 4 March. The residents had raised concerns about the proposed lighting scheme; the matter had been referred to the Estates Sub-Committee for review.

The forum had focused on long-term water resource planning and the regional water grid proposals. She noted that NMWA's position on the proposed grid interconnection had been well received, and that further consultation documents were expected from the regulator in April.

3.2 The Chair also reported that she had received a letter from the local MP regarding the recent billing system upgrade. The MP had raised constituent concerns about the accuracy of some bills issued in early March. The Chair had responded confirming that the issue was being investigated by the Customer Services team and that a full report would be provided to the board at the April meeting.

**4. Financial report - D. Thompson**

4.1 D. Thompson presented the financial report for the period ending 28 February 2026. He reported that the revenue position was broadly in line with the budget, with a small favourable variance of £0.4m, primarily attributable to lower than anticipated energy costs at the treatment works.

4.2 D. Thompson noted that the capital programme expenditure was running at 78% of the annual budget as of the end of February. He advised that this was slightly ahead of the planned profile due to the early completion of the Littleford pumping station works, which had been reported to the board at the February meeting. He confirmed that the remaining capital projects were on track for completion by the year end.

4.3 The Chair queried the position on bad debt provision. D. Thompson confirmed that the provision remained at the level agreed at the December meeting, and that the quarterly review of aged debt had shown a slight improvement in the collection rate for domestic customers. He noted that the commercial debt position remained stable.

**5. Operational performance report - J. O'Neil**

**Present:** C. Whitfield (Chair), J. O'Neil, D. Thompson, P. Patel, M. Hussain, S. Chen (Secretary)
**Apologies:** R. Green, A. Kowalski

6.1 P. Patel presented the water quality report for the period January to February 2026. She confirmed that all 42 sampling points across the supply zone had been tested within the required frequency, and that there had been no breaches of the Water Supply (Water Quality) Regulations 2016 during the period.

6.2 P. Patel drew the board's attention to the ongoing work on the nitrate reduction programme at the Bracknell Road borehole. She reported that the pilot treatment trial had now been running for eight weeks, and that preliminary results showed a reduction in nitrate levels of approximately 15% from the raw water baseline. She advised that this was in line with the modelling predictions, and that a further update would be provided at the May meeting.

6.3 The Chair asked whether the recent dry weather had had any effect on raw water quality. P. Patel confirmed that there had been a slight elevation in turbidity at the River intake during the first week of March, but that this had not affected compliance. She noted that the treatment works had managed the event without any reduction in output.

6.4 **Resolved:** That the water quality report for the period January to February 2026 be noted.

**7. Customer service and billing update - S. Chen**

7.1 S. Chen presented an update on the billing system upgrade, following the letter from the local MP reported at item 3.2. She confirmed that the Customer Services team had completed a full review of all bills issued between 1 March and 14 March, and that the total number of affected accounts was 1,247.

7.2 S. Chen explained that the issue had been traced to a configuration error in the new direct debit calculation module, which had resulted in some customers being charged the wrong amount for the period. She confirmed that the error had been identified on 12 March and that a fix had been deployed on 15 March. All affected customers had been contacted, and the majority of the incorrect charges had been reversed or credited.

7.3 S. Chen reported that a small number of customers (approximately 40) had not yet received their corrected bills, due to a backlog in the printing queue. She advised that these would be issued by the end of the week, and that the Customer Services team would be making follow-up calls to each affected customer.

7.4 The Chair asked whether the error had been reported to the regulator. S. Chen confirmed that the Information Commissioner's Office had not been notified, as the error did not involve a data breach. She stated that the team had briefed the regulator's customer service team informally, and that a formal notification would be made if any customer remained dissatisfied after the corrections had been applied.

He advised that the contractor had been mobilised and that the traffic management plan had been approved by the local authority. He noted that the works were expected to take eight weeks, and that there would be some disruption to local businesses during the period.

documents.title: NMWA Board Meeting Minutes - March 2026
documents.content:
**2. Matters arising**

2.1 The Chair noted that the revised drought management plan had been circulated to all board members by email on 9 March. Members were asked to submit any final comments to the Company Secretary by 25 March. No further action was required at this meeting.

2.2 S. Chen reported that the trial of the new telemetry units at the Hazelwood booster station had been completed. The units were functioning within specification. A full report would be circulated with the April papers.

2.3 P. Patel confirmed that the results of the February raw water sampling at the River Lune intake had been received and filed. No exceedances were recorded. This item was noted.

**3. Chair's remarks**

The Chair welcomed members and noted that the company had experienced a demanding start to the year, with the cold weather in January followed by an unseasonably mild February. He thanked operational staff for their continued efforts. He also noted that the company had received a number of customer compliments regarding the handling of the burst main on the B6254 in early March, and asked that these be passed on to the relevant crews.

**4. Operational update – S. Chen**

4.1 S. Chen presented a summary of operational performance for February and the first half of March. Key points:

- Water production for February was 2.1% below forecast, largely due to the mild weather reducing demand.
- The number of customer contacts regarding supply interruptions was within the target range.
- The planned maintenance programme at the Luneside treatment works was on schedule.
- The new sludge dewatering centrifuge at the same site had been commissioned and was operating at 92% availability during its first week, which was below the expected 95%. The manufacturer had been notified and a service visit was arranged for the week of 23 March.

The board minutes note that the Algae Bloom Incident reported_to_regulator was 2026-03-16. Record status: historical.

4.2 The Chair asked whether the centrifuge issue posed any compliance risk. S. Chen replied that it did not; the standby centrifuge remained available and there was sufficient sludge storage capacity on site. J. O'Neil added that the issue appeared to be a sensor fault rather than a mechanical problem, but this had not yet been confirmed.

4.3 S. Chen drew the board's attention to the forthcoming annual mains flushing programme, which would begin in the northern zone in April. Customers in the affected areas would be notified by leaflet and via the website. She noted that the programme had been coordinated with the local council to avoid clashing with road resurfacing works.

**5. Water quality update – P. Patel**

5.1 P. Patel provided an update on water quality monitoring for the period. Routine samples had been taken across all supply zones, and all regulatory parameters were within the required standards.

5.2 She also reported on the outcome of a recent external audit of the company's sampling procedures, which had been conducted in February. The audit had found no non-conformities, although two minor observations had been raised regarding the labelling of sample bottles at one remote site. These had been addressed immediately.

5.3 The Chair thanked P. Patel for the update.

**6. Financial report – M. Ellis**

6.1 M. Ellis presented the management accounts for the period ended 28 February 2026. Headline figures:

- Revenue was 1.4% ahead of budget, due to higher than expected non-household consumption.
- Operating costs were 0.8% below budget, mainly due to lower energy costs.
- Capital expenditure was 61% of the year-to-date budget, with slippage on two minor projects. M. Ellis noted that the slippage was not expected to impact the year-end position.

documents.title: NMWA Board Meeting Minutes - March 2026
documents.content:
**7. Network performance and maintenance update – Operations Director**

7.1 The Operations Director provided an update on the performance of the Northbridge Water Network for the period to the end of March 2026. Overall network performance was reported as satisfactory, with no unplanned supply interruptions recorded during the month.

7.2 The total number of reported leaks on the Northbridge Water Network for 2026 was noted. The Operations Director reported that the Northbridge Water Network reported_leak_count_2026 is 27. Record status: current. This figure is current and has been logged in the network asset management system. He noted that this compared with 31 for the same period in 2025, representing a reduction of approximately 13%.

7.3 The Chair asked whether the reduction was attributable to the proactive leak detection programme which had been trialled in the eastern zone during the winter. The Operations Director confirmed that this was partly the case, but cautioned that the milder winter weather had also been a factor. He reminded the board that the trial had been extended to the southern zone in March and that a full evaluation would be presented at the June meeting.

7.4 In response to a question from the Chair regarding the age profile of the network, the Operations Director noted that a significant proportion of the network was of cast iron construction and over 50 years old. He confirmed that the capital maintenance programme was targeting the highest risk sections and that a condition assessment of the remaining sections would be completed by the end of the year.

7.5 The board noted the update and asked that the full network performance report, including the leak data, be circulated to members with the minutes.

**8. Mains flushing programme**

8.1 The Operations Director reminded the board that the annual mains flushing programme would commence in the northern zone on 20 April 2026. He confirmed that all customer notifications had been dispatched and that the programme had been coordinated with the local council to minimise disruption.

8.2 He reported that the flushing programme was expected to take six weeks to complete, subject to weather conditions. Any customer complaints arising during the programme would be logged and reviewed at the next monthly meeting.

**9. Customer service report – S. Chen**

9.1 S. Chen presented the customer service performance report for the period January to March 2026. Key indicators were as follows:

- Complaints received: 214, compared with 238 in the same period last year.
- Average response time to written complaints: 5.2 working days, against a target of 10 working days.
- Calls answered within 30 seconds: 78%, against a target of 85%. S. Chen noted that the shortfall was due to a temporary staffing issue in the call centre during February, which had now been resolved.

9.2 The Chair noted the improvement in complaint numbers and asked whether any particular issue had driven the reduction. S. Chen advised that the new online reporting form, introduced in January, had made it easier for customers to report problems such as leaks and low pressure, and that this had improved the accuracy of the initial data received.

**10. Any other business**

10.1 The Chair advised that the company had received an invitation to participate in a regional water efficiency forum, organised by the Environment Agency. It was agreed that the Operations Director would attend, and he would report back to the board in June.

10.2 There being no further business, the Chair closed the meeting at 15:40.

**Date of next meeting:** 20 May 2026, at 10:00.

**NMWA Board Meeting Minutes - March 2026**

**Held on 17 March 2026 at NMWA Head Office, 10:00 - 12:30**

**Present:** C. Whitfield (Chair), J. O'Neil, D. Thompson, P. Patel, M. Hussain, S. Chen (Secretary)
**Apologies:** R. Green, A. Kowalski

**6. Water quality and environmental compliance - P. Patel**

6.1 P. Patel presented the water quality report for the period January to February 2026. She confirmed that all 42 sampling points across the supply zone had been tested within the required frequency, and that there had been no breaches of the Water Supply (Water Quality) Regulations 2016 during the period.

6.2 P. Patel drew the board's attention to the ongoing work on the nitrate reduction programme at the Bracknell Road borehole. She reported that the pilot treatment trial had now been running for eight weeks, and that preliminary results showed a reduction in nitrate levels of approximately 15% from the raw water baseline. She advised that this was in line with the modelling predictions, and that a further update would be provided at the May meeting.

6.3 The Chair asked whether the recent dry weather had had any effect on raw water quality. P. Patel confirmed that there had been a slight elevation in turbidity at the River intake during the first week of March, but that this had not affected compliance. She noted that the treatment works had managed the event without any reduction in output.

6.4 **Resolved:** That the water quality report for the period January to February 2026 be noted.

**7. Customer service and billing update - S. Chen**

7.1 S. Chen presented an update on the billing system upgrade, following the letter from the local MP reported at item 3.2. She confirmed that the Customer Services team had completed a full review of all bills issued between 1 March and 14 March, and that the total number of affected accounts was 1,247.

7.2 S. Chen explained that the issue had been traced to a configuration error in the new direct debit calculation module, which had resulted in some customers being charged the wrong amount for the period. She confirmed that the error had been identified on 12 March and that a fix had been deployed on 15 March. All affected customers had been contacted, and the majority of the incorrect charges had been reversed or credited.

7.3 S. Chen reported that a small number of customers (approximately 40) had not yet received their corrected bills, due to a backlog in the printing queue. She advised that these would be issued by the end of the week, and that the Customer Services team would be making follow-up calls to each affected customer.

7.4 The Chair asked whether the error had been reported to the regulator. S. Chen confirmed that the Information Commissioner's Office had not been notified, as the error did not involve a data breach. She stated that the team had briefed the regulator's customer service team informally, and that a formal notification would be made if any customer remained dissatisfied after the corrections had been applied.

7.5 **Resolved:** That the update on the billing system upgrade be noted, and that a further report be provided at the April meeting.

**8. Capital programme and project update - J. O'Neil**

8.1 J. O'Neil presented an update on the capital programme, as at the end of February 2026. He confirmed that the Littleford pumping station works had been substantially completed on 26 February, ahead of the planned completion date of 15 March. He reported that the site had been handed back to the operations team on 2 March, and that the final snagging list was being worked through.

8.2 J. O'Neil reported that the next major project, the replacement of the water main on High Street, was due to commence on 6 April. He advised that the contractor had been mobilised and that the traffic management plan had been approved by the local authority. He noted that the works were expected to take eight weeks, and that there would be some disruption to local businesses during the period.
